subject: Clarify SOC2 coverage for VPC/on-prem (bridge letter & KMS)
messages:

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finexa.com>

Subject: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter question for VPC/on-prem

Hi Aisha,

Hope you’re well — Finexa's procurement and security teams are reviewing Redwood as part of a planned production rollout. Two quick questions we need documented before we can move to PO:

1) Audit period: will your SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 28 Feb 2025 cover an audit window that aligns with our contract start (we expect go-live in Mar 2026)? If not, will Redwood provide a bridge letter for the period between the report end date and our contract start?

2) Scope: we need clarity about which deployment modes are covered. Specifically: hosted API (clear), dedicated reserved pools (we have a large reserved cluster request), and customer VPC / on-prem (Finexa requires that private VPC endpoints and on-prem connectors be included in attestation or accompanied by a bridge letter).

Can you confirm whether the SOC 2 covers dedicated pools and whether you will provide a bridge letter that explicitly states coverage (or limitations) for VPC/on-prem connectors and KMS arrangements? We also need a short list of the evidence artifacts you can share (tenant isolation diagram, KMS configuration statements, network egress IP ranges).

Thanks — if easier, we can schedule a 30-min technical call.

Regards,
Alice Moran
Senior Sourcing Manager, Finexa

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Vivek (security) and Monica (sales ops) to confirm artifacts and next steps. Quick answers up front so you have something to ingest today:

- Audit period: our most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers 03/01/2024 — 02/28/2025. We can provide that Type II report now (attached) and we offer a bridge letter that documents applicable controls and any exceptions for the period after 02/28/2025 up to contract start.

- Scope: Hosted API endpoints are fully in-scope for the SOC 2 report. Dedicated reserved pools (where customers have reserved capacity in our Dedicated product) are included when the customer is provisioned in an isolated tenant within a dedicated pool that we map during the audit sampling. For private VPC/on-prem connectors, the standard SOC 2 does not automatically cover customer-managed infrastructure (on-prem or air-gapped). We can provide a bridge letter stating which Redwood controls continue to apply to the control plane operations and what evidence we can supply for customer-managed components.

I attached the SOC 2 PDF and a bridge letter template for your legal/security review. Vivek — can you confirm the list of artifacts Finexa requested and whether we need IP ranges or a more detailed tenant isolation diagram? Monica — I'll need a short statement for procurement about how dedicated pool membership is sampled during audit.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter question for VPC/on-prem

Paul, Alice — diving into technical specifics to make the bridge letter and artifacts useful:

1) Dedicated pools and sampling: Our external auditor samples by tenant identifier. For Dedicated reservations we map the customer's tenant ID(s) to the pool and confirm whether any of those tenant IDs were included in the auditor's sample window. We cannot disclose auditor working papers, but we can provide:
  - a tenant mapping statement (which tenant IDs are in your reserved pool),
  - confirmation whether any of those tenant IDs were part of the auditor sample for the 03/01/2024-02/28/2025 report, and
  - a short note describing our isolation controls (logical tenancy, network ACLs at hypervisor/orchestrator layer). See attached tenant_isolation_diagram.png.

2) KMS and VPC/on-prem: When customers use customer-managed KMS keys, root-of-trust for the encryption keys is in the customer's account — Redwood operates integrations that never store plaintext customer keys. For SOC 2 purposes:
  - We can attest (in the bridge letter) that Redwood's control activities around KMS integrations (key usage logging, access control policies, rotation practices on our side) were tested.
  - We will explicitly call out limitations: any key lifecycle operations and physical security for the KMS in the customer's account are out of scope for Redwood's SOC 2.
  - For private link / on-prem connectors, we can document the supported network topology and provide egress IP ranges and TLS configuration expectations. If Finexa requires testing evidence inside your environment (e.g., packet captures or KMS policy snapshots), that will need to be handled as a customer-supplied artifact or via an agreed third-party attestation.

3) Next steps we recommend:
  - Finexa to share the tenant IDs you plan to use and the KMS key ARNs.
  - We'll produce a short bridge letter (1–2 pages) that: references the SOC 2 report, lists supported artifacts we can provide, and states control limitations for customer-managed pieces.
  - Schedule a 30-min technical call (Vivek + Aisha + Finexa security) to walk through mappings.

Happy to draft the bridge letter language for legal review if you send the tenant IDs.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
